correctness.rationale: The stated 2024 DSR home-plus-away score is specialized explicitly to strict tournaments, with both active partition conditions and the empty-successor case. We independently wrote a C implementation of the score separate from the source dsr_verify.c, compiled it and enumerated without pruning every integer bit encoding of each labeled tournament n=2,...,7. Failure counts were exactly 0,0,0,0,0,5040 out of 2,8,64,1024,32768,2097152; first failure is bit mask 1324. The witness scores were independently recovered as DSR (6,3,2,4,5,14,14) and Copeland (3,3,2,2,2,5,4). A separate independent 7! permutation-orbit enumeration found 5040 distinct relabelings of witness 1324, hence trivial automorphism group; original package code checks all 5040 failures lie in that orbit. These exact finite exhaustive checks establish the bound n<=7, not arbitrary larger tournaments. Primary 2024 source Proposition 7 and scoring equations were inspected.

originality.rationale: Hou 2024 Sections 4 and 6.3 established up-to-four containment, reported five-case verification and posed a general Copeland refinement conjecture. The new bit-coded exhaustive first failure at seven and unique asymmetric isomorphism class refutes that exact 2024 rule. The 2025 journal abstract repeats the smaller guarantee; a 2026 DSR tournament solution uses a different scoring version, and its full text could not be accessed due to VPN disconnection. Resultary seven-alternative Banks/uncovered census concerns different tournament correspondences and does not cover this DSR/Copeland condition. Qualified PASS, with a precise risk of an already-known counterexample in 2025/2026 follow-ups.
